title: DC-area forecast: Stellar today and then a steady warming trend
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Enjoy the sunny and warm afternoon, with highs of 80 to 85.

What’s next? Staying sunny through midweek as humidity gradually increases and highs approach 90. Thursday brings the next chance of showers and storms.

Today’s daily digit — 9/10: The warm sunshine is an outstanding way to cap the holiday weekend. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Monday): With plentiful sunshine, highs this afternoon climb to 80 to 85. Humidity levels are low to moderate, with dew points near 60. Winds are light from the north at around 5 mph. Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tonight: Partly cloudy and pleasant. Evening 70s fall back to the mid-60s downtown and the upper 50s to low 60s in most other places. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Tuesday): Still sunny and a little warmer and more humid than Monday, with dew points in the low 60s. Highs reach the mid- to upper 80s with light winds from the southwest. Confidence: High

Tomorrow night: Partly cloudy with a hint of mugginess. Overall, though, it’s a nice early September night, with lows in the 60s and light winds from the south. Confidence: High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

It’s more of a midsummer pattern by midweek, with sunshine pushing highs close to 90 by Wednesday. It’s more humid as well, with dew points in the mid-60s. Thursday is the week’s muggiest day, with highs near 90 and dew points near 70. As a cold front approaches, showers and storms are possible, and some could be strong. Lows Wednesday and Thursday are in the 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Medium-High

It’s not as toasty on Friday, with mostly sunny skies and highs of 80 to 85. The weekend then looks partly sunny and warm, with highs well into the 80s. Nighttime lows are mostly in the 60s. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 7

Extreme heat in 1881 sent temperatures to a record 104 degrees, while in 1934 a soaking storm brought record rainfall and widespread flooding across the city.
